issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
fix: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

issue: League Gothic is the display face of appmeta-pulse-b (the banner) and of soon-b (the event title and the stub's big value).
fix: soon-b keeps it, since Alternate Gothic is the ticket/event-poster face. appmeta-pulse-b sets its banner in Libre Franklin 900: the Franklin Gothic of US markets pages, and already its text family. That makes Franklin a display face in appmeta-pulse-b, so allpaid-c moves its window headline and indicia caps off Libre Franklin (e.g. Epilogue 600/800, unused on the board).

issue: Exact Steps Only shares Dela Gothic One (display) with shogiful-b. Its amber Doto dot-matrix numerals on black duplicate soon-c's countdown board (#FFB23F vs #FFB21E, both Doto 700), and Doto then sits in three surfaces. Its 'INSERT 2,026 STEPS' credit display is the same object as earnlock-c's giant remaining-steps count, so a and c lead with one move. Its own risk line also calls the machine a hero-only device with plain panels below, which makes it a hero skin.
fix: Dela Gothic One goes to shogiful-b, whose subject is Japanese. Set the marquee in Mochiy Pop One, a Japanese sticker/marquee gothic unused elsewhere. Make all price lamps lighting together the one move, and shrink the credit display to a small red 7-segment strip, as on real machines. That drops Doto here and leaves it on chessful-a and soon-c. Below the hero, keep the page on machine faces (side-panel plates, the audit printout, the pickup bin) instead of plain set panels.

issue: Three White Lights is the split hero in costume. The H1, subheadline and a badge/price/QR slip are stacked on the left, and a device (the black judging console) fills the right. Its ground (#d5e3ec bench-card blue + #121619 ink + red) is wanderwiki-a's aerogramme palette (#DCE6F1 + #15223D + #C4232D). It also echoes soon-c's pale blue-grey console with one black instrument.
fix: Run the light board across the full width as the stage, with the three lenses large and the verdict strip under them. Set the H1 above it and the hand-in slip below it. Ground the page in its white form paper (#FBFBF9), so the black housing is the only mass.

issue: Atlas of Nights is the literal reading on a navy plate (#0E1C3A) set in Atkinson Next + Atkinson Mono. In the same body trio, aftershift-a is navy twill (#18222F) set in Atkinson Next + Atkinson Mono. Stars on navy are also the sleep category's moon-and-stars default and soon-a's night band. Its furniture (a high-contrast Didone, spaced capitals laid along hairlines, small mono axis labels on a fine grid) is AI cluster (c) in an astronomy costume.
fix: aftershift-a keeps navy and Atkinson: the uniform colour and the low-acuity argument are literal. observa-a takes its icon's own warm night (~#15110F), with apricot as the only colour and no glow. Constellation names and labels move into one sans with tabular figures (e.g. League Spartan, from the Futura lineage of star charts), with no mono and no spaced Didone caps. Keep Bodoni Moda for the H1 at most.

issue: First Light's hero is a centred iPhone rising behind a sun disc, with the headline and subheadline flanking it. That is the category's phone-mockup hero (and the incumbent's phone) on a symmetrical axis. The world sits behind the product as scenery, and its star field on indigo duplicates observa-a's sky.
fix: Make the backward schedule the first-viewport object. Set T-90, T-30, T-14, T-3 and T-1 on the twilight bands themselves, from astronomical twilight to sunrise, with the day at the horizon. Put the badge on the horizon and move the phone below the fold into the civil band. Drop the star field entirely.

issue: Both lead with the hero-metric template inside an instrument. earnlock-c sets '3,412' at 232px with a small 'STEPS / UNTIL UNLOCK' label and a right-hand column of three stat rows (steps · Free / min · Premium / kcal · Premium). soon-c sets 'T-30' at 240px over a task line and a row of three labelled status lamps.
fix: earnlock-c keeps the single count. MODE cycles steps → minutes → kcal in that same segment field, the fixed LCD icon segments act as its label, and the three-row stat column leaves the first viewport. soon-c drops the status-lamp row from the hero: the board shows one T-time and its task, and the EARLIER/LATER keys are its only furniture.

issue: Held Over (a cinema marquee with a box office and a ticket tray) and soon-b 'Admit One' (the event ticket) are one world, going to the show, inside the planning pair. Its author also ranks it the weakest planning link (#7). It carries the Big Shoulders family (shared with studio-a and gymlogger-x-a), and its amber bulbs on a navy fascia join both the amber-on-dark cluster and the navy cluster.
fix: Replace it with taskful-day candidate #5, the felt letterboard with push-in letters. It keeps the dealt changeable-letter 'held over' mechanic in a domestic object with no tickets. Set its letters in a face outside the Big Shoulders family, as white letters on a coloured felt rather than amber bulbs on navy.

issue: Admit One's ticket card (#F3C6D2, 'cherry-blossom pink') is the same pale pink as shogiful-c's first newsprint signature (#F3CBD2). Its sakura reading also points at the Japanese costume that Shogiful's category default warns against.
fix: shogiful-c keeps the pink, because tinted manga signatures are native to it. Print soon-b's ticket on a stock no other surface uses, e.g. pale aqua card (~#C4E6E1). Keep the aubergine ink and the app-blue spot, and re-check blue text on the new stock for 4.5:1.

issue: Literata is chessful-b's display and text face and soon-a's text and figure face.
fix: chessful-b keeps it. Give soon-a a reading serif no other style uses, e.g. Petrona 400/600 with tabular lining figures.

issue: Both planning apps offer a timer instrument: taskful-day-c's wind-up dial set to 25, and soon-c's T-minus board stepping through T-times.
fix: These are acceptable as different objects. If both are chosen, keep taskful-day-c light and round (the top-down dial) and soon-c's board rectangular, and never give taskful-day-c a digital readout.

issue: Raster weight is unbudgeted everywhere. Every microsite puts the app icon in its nav or hero at 24 to 72px, and most put screenshots in carousels or heroes. The only files that exist are 1024px icon PNGs of 0.56 to 3.96 MB (mediakit.png is 3.96 MB; lagerland-mark.png is 1.96 MB, and the current header already ships it at 30px) and 1206x2622 screenshot PNGs of 0.3 to 7.6 MB (soon/2.png is 7.6 MB, mediakit/2.png is 7.1 MB). Nearly every card says assetsNeeded: none, so no style accounts for derivatives. Shipped as-is, a 390px page downloads several MB before the badge is usable.
fix: Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

issue: LCP risk: all three heroes make a screenshot PNG the likely LCP element. Style a's rising phone uses 1.png (6.97 MB). Style b's art panel is a crop of 2.png (7.6 MB). Style c's monitor bay is a crop of 3.png (6.1 MB). 'A crop from the existing PNG' means either CSS-cropping a 7 MB file on a phone, or making a new raster that no card lists.
fix: List the hero image as a needed asset: a committed WebP/AVIF crop at 2x display size (a: about 600x1300 and 90 KB or less; b: a 780x440 mobile crop and a 680x1330 desktop crop; c: about 600x760). Preload it with fetchpriority=high and give it explicit width/height. In style a, run the 40px rise as a transform from full opacity, so it never delays the LCP paint.

issue: Sticky bars hide focus (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.4.11). Every style adds a sticky download bar after the hero, and most also pin a top strip; earnlock-c also fixes side rims, shogiful-a keeps a tag rail and soon-a an earth bar. A focused link, FAQ summary or #anchor target can land underneath them. On a Safari viewport of about 664px, two 52 to 64px bars plus the Smart App Banner can cover more than a quarter of the screen.
fix: Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

issue: On mobile the badge is below the visible fold: style a puts it on the earth at y580 to 760, style b on the stub at y630 to 760.
fix: Style a: set the badge and price line under the headline (about y240 to 300) and let the phone rise from the arc beneath them; the arc can still carry the 'no ads' line. Style b: cut the art panel to about 140px and set the title at 52px, or put the 'ADMIT ONE' price and badge row directly under the title (about y480) with the T-fields after it.

issue: Shared display face: B612 sets soon-c's headline and legends and is also appmeta-pulse-a's display.
fix: Keep B612 (plus B612 Mono) on appmeta-pulse-a. Drop B612 from soon-c and set the headline and engraved legends in Public Sans 700 caps. Public Sans is already soon-c's text face, and as the US government's open face it suits a launch console; this also saves about 34 KB.

issue: Shared display face: League Gothic is also appmeta-pulse-b's display. Its text face, Sofia Sans, is used on three surfaces (mediakit-a, pawza-a, soon-b).
fix: Keep League Gothic on appmeta-pulse-b (newspaper listings). Move soon-b to Anton 400 (a show-bill gothic, 18 KB) for the title, fares and stub numerals, and Kumbh Sans 400/700 (13 KB each) for body and field labels, with Kumbh's tabular figures for prices and T-times.

issue: Layout shift from huge display headlines. Many heroes set 100 to 128px condensed or expanded H1s (millrace-c Antonio at 128px, soon-b at 128px, allpaid-a at 112px, gymlogger-x-a at 112px, liftlog-a at wdth 125). When the font swaps in from a system fallback with very different widths, the H1 reflows and the hero shifts.
fix: For each display face, declare a metric-matched fallback @font-face (size-adjust, ascent-override and descent-override over a local system face), preload only the display file, and use font-display: swap for text faces and optional for the giant H1 face.

issue: Shared text face: Literata is the display and text face of chessful-b (Move by Move), where the whole book world rests on it.
fix: Set soon-a's text in Petrona 400/600 (about 23 KB each, tabular lining figures available), and leave Literata to chessful-b.

issue: Once started, RUN THE COUNT advances every 1.6s with no stop control, and each lamp change risks a fresh live-region announcement.
fix: While running, the RUN THE COUNT key becomes STOP (aria-pressed). Announce through aria-live=polite only when a milestone is reached, not on every digit fade.

issue: The Ticket classes table stamps Premium Annual 'Best value'. The front matter gives Annual only highlight: true and no label. With Lifetime at $12.99 once against Annual at $9.99/yr, 'Best value' on the yearly plan is misleading after about 16 months.
fix: Mark Annual with a neutral in-world mark (a punched hole or a 'Billed yearly' line). If the owner wants a value stamp, add an approved highlight_label to the front matter first; 'Best long-term value' would belong on Lifetime.

issue: Countdown sequence: six engraved template keys select which milestone table 'prints'. The no-JS fallback named is only the trip board plus 'the full milestone table' for that one template. Wedding, Pregnancy, Birthday, Graduation and Move (5 of the 6 example_insights) have no stated no-JS fallback.
fix: Server-render all six milestone tables as visible, crawlable tables. The keys should only scroll to or highlight a table and drive the board.

issue: Both print all six templates without JS, but with JS a's type switcher and b's 'Print your ticket' reprint a single template in their place. Rendering crawlers and JS visitors then lose 5 of the 6.
fix: Keep the six server-rendered template rows visible when JS runs. The interactive ticket adds a personalised seventh above them instead of replacing them.

issue: The trust line 'iOS · 0 third-party SDKs · no ads · no account · events stay on your iPhone' sits in the hero, the stub or the shelf with no transparency link.
fix: Make the trust line the link to /transparency/#soon.

issue: On mobile the stub with fare and badge starts at y≈630 and the badge lands at about y700-750, under Safari's toolbar on load.
fix: On phones put the stub (fare and badge) right after the title, before the T-field row.
